context.scenario: Optionally mapping a fresh repo into a Graphify knowledge graph
context.description: The user just dropped the kit into a repo. initialize Phase 0 offers the whole-project map; the user's answer (and whether Graphify is installed) decides whether graphify-map runs. Default is prefer.
context.note: graphify-map is strictly optional: it must check installation before running, must not install Graphify without asking, and must treat a non-clear-no as prefer.

evals.title: Graphify not installed — check first, offer install, never silently install
evals.prompt: The user prefers to map the project with Graphify, but `command -v graphify` finds nothing and no Graphify skill exists on the host.
expectations: the skill detects Graphify is missing before attempting to run anything
it shows the user the project URL (https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify) and offers to install (uv tool install graphifyy or pip install graphifyy)
it does NOT install without the user's explicit go-ahead, and does NOT pretend to run the map
if the user declines the install, the map is skipped cleanly with no error state

evals.title: Default is prefer — a non-clear-no proceeds
evals.prompt: Graphify is installed. The user answers the preference question with 'whatever, your call' (not a clear no).
expectations: the skill treats a non-clear-no as prefer (the default) — it does not require an explicit yes
it runs the Graphify pipeline on the project root (the repo being mapped, not the kit folder)
output is written under graphify-out/ at the project root (graph.json + GRAPH_REPORT.md + HTML viz)
it reports where the map lives and points later codebase questions at `graphify query`

evals.title: Clear no — stop cleanly, never block
evals.prompt: The user answers the preference question with 'no thanks'. Graphify is installed.
expectations: the skill stops without running the pipeline
it says the map is skipped and can be re-run anytime (no blocking, no error)
it does not install or configure anything

evals.title: Multiple targets — clone/extract each, merge into one cross-repo graph
evals.prompt: The user prefers the map and names two extra targets: a GitHub URL (a sibling service) and a local folder ./libs/. Graphify is installed.
expectations: the GitHub URL is handled via `graphify clone` (clones into ~/.graphify/repos/<owner>/<repo>, reused on repeat runs)
the local folder is handled via `graphify extract <path>` per folder — NOT the skill pipeline per folder (which writes to the CWD's graphify-out/ and clobbers)
all targets' graph.json files are merged with `graphify merge-graphs ... --out graphify-out/graph.json` at the project root — exactly that out path, since the query fast path checks it
the report mentions merged nodes carry a `repo` attribute so queries can filter by origin
